description: HELD-OUT copycats -- TEST ONLY, NEVER TRAIN. Close copies of the eight games our team holds out of all training. Each keeps one original game's rules and level-by-level progression (the original rule code drives every step) and changes maps, colours, sprite art, HUD position and, where the code allows, tile size. Every level ships with a winning line proven in the engine and through arc_agi's offline loader. Never mix with the 17-game copycat package.
usage: TEST ONLY -- NEVER TRAIN. Held-out evaluation copy of a held-out game.

games.usage: TEST ONLY -- NEVER TRAIN. Held-out evaluation copy of a held-out game.
games.name: Axis Reflectors held-out copycat
games.kept: ar25's class drives every step (renamed and subclassed): arrows move the selected piece or mirror one cell (vertical mirrors only sideways, horizontal only up/down), cycle and click select, undo, live reflections across every mirror, a level ends when every target cell is covered, per-level step budget; eight levels with the same pieces, mirrors and mirror kinds, and budgets.
games.changed: Every board mirrored or half-turned (the transforms that keep vertical mirrors vertical); a new target shape on every level, made from what a new arrangement of the movable parts covers, at least as far from the start as the original's own solution, with every piece and movable mirror needed; levels 1-2 certified by exact search (fewest steps 15/15 and 12/11, copy/original); step bar moved from the right column to the left; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Tile scale: the rules' own overlay only draws at the 21-cell board's scale. Piece art: the rules read piece pixels. Levels 3-8 are not certified by search (two pieces and two mirrors are too many states); their difficulty bound is the displacement of the intended arrangement.

games.usage: TEST ONLY -- NEVER TRAIN. Held-out evaluation copy of a held-out game.
games.name: Always Sliding held-out copycat
games.kept: The as66 recreation's rule code unchanged: sliding blocks on a wrapping field, patrolling enemies that step first and kill on contact, recolour bars, cups with colour markers, free repeat press of the lit side, per-level move meter; nine levels with the same piece inventory per level.
games.changed: Every map new (searched and proven): grid sizes, walls, piece placement, cup openings, bar orientation; one colour permutation for all roles; cell size per level changed; notched blocks, hollow enemies, open ring corners; move meter from the bottom, progress bar on the top row.
games.not_changed: Nothing in the rules. Enemy levels are only required to let an enemy kill within the first moves, not to block the obvious line the way a hand-made level would.

games.name: Reach Emblems held-out copycat
games.kept: re86's class drives every step (renamed and subclassed): arrows slide the selected piece three pixels, ACTION5 passes control, pieces pass through each other, colour pads repaint, walls bend crosses and squash hollow squares, a level clears when every dot's centre is covered by a piece of its colour, per-level step budget; eight levels with the same pieces, pads, walls and budgets.
games.changed: Every level turned or mirrored (a square symmetry under which the original's own winning line still clears); new dots on every level -- each piece is driven (over a pad of a new colour where the original forces repainting) to a new resting place at least as far in total from the start as the original solution moves them, and the dots are stamped on the pieces as they finally lie, in the original's number, never on a pixel already right at the start; step bar moved from the bottom row to the top row; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Tile scale: the rules move pieces three pixels on a fixed 64-pixel board. Piece, pad and wall art: the rules read their pixels. Difficulty is bounded by the intended displacement, not certified by search.

games.name: Sequence Belt held-out copycat
games.kept: sb26's rule code: pick up / place / swap tiles, run reads the first machine against the goal row, rings jump into the machine of their colour and nest or loop, 64 energy, undo; eight levels with the same machines, fixed pieces and tray inventory per level.
games.changed: Smaller tiles on a 5-pixel slot pitch (was 6) with 3x3 colour (was 4x4); new ring, slot and frame art; all pieces recoloured; the intended arrangement shuffled so every goal row is new (same number of distinct colours and ring jumps or more); machines re-laid out, tray re-ordered, goal block moved; energy bar moved to the left column; dark theme.
games.not_changed: Level 2's one-off line joining the ring to its machine is left out. Goal squares keep the original's 7-pixel pitch because the twelve-goal failure bar is hard-wired to it. One render-only guard keeps the match flash inside the smaller tiles.

games.name: Sucking Up held-out copycat
games.kept: su15's class drives every step (renamed and subclassed): click pulls nearby pieces onto the click, same-tier clusters merge up the size chain, mixed-tier collisions are fouls with escalating penalties, creatures chase and shrink blocks, exact deliveries into circles, header rows refuse clicks; nine levels with the same pieces, creatures, targets, budgets and shopping lists.
games.changed: Every level mirrored left-to-right (legends move to the right of the header); every playfield reworked -- blocks, creatures and circles nudged to new spots and up to three decoy blocks added, keeping only edits under which the original's winning clicks, mirrored, still clear exactly on the last click; step bar moved from the bottom row to the right column; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Tile scale: the rules hard-code the 64x64 field (click maths, header rows, pull reach). Block shapes: tiers are told apart by size and colour and catching tests piece pixels. On level 7 the mirrored clicks sit one pixel further left, because the pull rounds piece centres.

games.name: Toggle Runes held-out copycat
games.kept: tr87's rule code: bracket moves left/right, up/down cycles a glyph (or a whole rule half on editable-rule levels), source must translate rule by rule into the target, same move budget; six levels with the same flags on the same levels and the same rule shapes.
games.changed: 21 new glyph shapes, 4x4 on a 6-pixel pitch (was 5x5 on 7); smaller family tiles; colours permuted; rule cards re-packed and panel divider moved; new rule sets and source rows on levels 1-4, new intended rules, source and target on level 5; new rotation and scramble seeds; budget bar moved to the left column.
games.not_changed: Level 6 keeps the original puzzle up to a cyclic relabelling of each glyph family (new glyph art, layout and scramble); a fresh level 6 needs a solver for the combined tree + two-step + editable-rule check that was not written.

games.name: Trail Unwind held-out copycat
games.kept: tu93's class drives every step (renamed and subclassed): arrow moves along wires pad to pad, enemies of each kind move after you and burst or kill on contact as in the original, green exit, per-level step budget; nine levels with the same enemies per level.
games.changed: Every level turned a quarter turn clockwise (headings turn with it); every board reworked -- dead-end branches grown and unused wires cut, only where the original's winning line, turned, still clears exactly on its last move (so no level gets easier); pads drawn as hollow rings; boards re-positioned in their views and level 4 drawn at twice the scale; step bar moved from the bottom row to the top row; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Tile scale on the other eight levels: boards are 33-45 pixels, so the engine can only draw them one pixel per cell. Token and enemy art: the rules read those sprites' pixels.

games.name: Volume Control held-out copycat
games.kept: vc33's class drives every step (renamed and subclassed): click a pump to push liquid through a wall, liquid settles toward the level's gravity side, riders on the surface must line up with the mark of their colour, ferries carry riders across, per-level click budget; seven levels with the same tanks, pumps, riders, ferries and budgets.
games.changed: Every level turned (quarter, half or three-quarter turn) with its gravity; new goals on levels 1-3 and 6 -- the marks move to rider positions the search first reaches no sooner than the original's fewest clicks, and the copy's fewest clicks, measured by breadth-first search in the engine, are >= the original's (4/3, 9/7, 24/23, 21/20); levels 1-2 drawn at half the tile size; views re-padded; budget bar moved from the top row to the bottom row; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Levels 4, 5 and 7 keep the original goal (turned): on level 4 no other rider position is as far from the start (searched exhaustively); levels 5 and 7 are too large to certify a new goal's difficulty. Level 6 is shifted, not turned: its rules special-case leftward gravity of strength 3. Pump, rider and ferry art unchanged: the rules read rider pixels and click hits.
